beats.text: Hedy Lamarr did not invent Wi-Fi.
beats.note: Her 1942 patent covered a radio guidance system for torpedoes. Earlier frequency-hopping patents exist, including US 1,598,673, granted in 1926.

beats.context: The patent proposed switching between 88 different carrier frequencies using perforated paper rolls, as in a player piano.

beats.note: US patent 2,292,387, filed on 10 June 1941 under her married name, Hedy Kiesler Markey, with the composer George Antheil.
The patent describes the remote control of torpedoes. Hopping between frequencies was meant to defeat jamming by Axis powers.

beats.text: It was not used in the war.
beats.note: Wikipedia says the Navy rejected it as too large to fit in a torpedo. Similar technology entered operational systems only in 1962, three years after the patent expired.

beats.text: Wi-Fi and Bluetooth use the same family of ideas. It is not her invention.
